newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH EXPORT BANK SEES EUROBOND IN FIRST HALF '97.
newsitem.headline: CZECH EXPORT BANK SEES EUROBOND IN FIRST HALF '97.

text.p: The Czech Export Bank (Ceska Exportni Banka) on Thursday said it expects to issue a $200-300 million, five-year Eurobond in the first half of 1997, lead-managed by investment bank J.P. Morgan.
Bank officials said funds from the loan will be used to help finance the bank's activities in extending export loans.

"We would like to finalise our entry to the market. A shareholders meeting has approved borrowing resources in the first half through a $200-300 million Eurobond," Tomas Revesz, the bank's general director told a news conference.
The Czech Export Banka (CEB), as of the end of 1996, has supported some 44 billion crowns worth of exports, and extended 8.66 billion crowns in actual loans.
The CEB was established in 1995 with a business mandate to increase Czech exports by providing exporters with competitive financing.

JP Morgan also arranged the CEB's only international fundraising exercise to date, a three-year, $185 million revolving credit which was signed in June, 1996. The loan was priced at 12.5 basis points above LIBOR.
